areas.summary: The Friends bubble in the companion menu gathers everything social: rooms you share with other Void Engine members, a playground where companions meet, and your own PCs. Rooms and friends' playdates run through the Void Engine rooms hub, which is not live for the public yet.

features.name: Friends bubble
features.what: One place in the companion menu for playdates, sharing rules, rooms and your PCs. A badge counts room invites, join requests and PC work waiting on you.
features.since: 0.4.0 (as a menu entry); the full Friends hub arrives in 0.4.5
features.evidence: renderer/companion-hub.js items list ('friends', 'Playdates, sharing, rooms and your PCs') and syncBadge(); v0.4.4 had only 'Your PCs, rooms and listening' (git show v0.4.4:renderer/companion-hub.js line 142); CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'The companion as a pet and a friend'

features.name: Friends › Rooms
features.what: Browse your rooms and listed rooms, ask to join with a short note, accept or decline invites, and let people in to rooms you own. Each room has a plain-text chat with @names.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Friends › Rooms'; README 'Community' (Rooms paragraph); renderer/rooms.js; commit 4ee6891 'Friends › Rooms: join, request, invite, decide and chat in Studio'. Needs the rooms hub address and a linked Discord (hub-client.cjs HUB_URL is empty on main)

features.name: Make a room
features.what: Start a Hangout room (up to 25 people) or a Cowork room (up to 10). Choose whether anyone can ask to join or it is invite-only, and whether it shows in the room list.
features.evidence: renderer/rooms.js create form ('Hangout (up to 25)', 'Cowork (up to 10)', 'Anyone can ask to join', 'Invite only', 'Show it in the room list'); Void Engine Bot docs/roles.md (Room Host role needed to create rooms)

features.name: Room owner controls
features.what: Invite people by name, lock a room so there are no new posts or requests, close it for everyone, or leave a room. Actions that cannot be undone ask twice.
features.evidence: renderer/rooms.js ('Invite someone: type a name', 'Lock', 'Close it for everyone?', 'Leave it?'); CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Actions that can't be undone ask twice'; commit e0951dd

features.name: Room chat safety
features.what: Links in room chat are never clickable, you can delete your own messages, and you can report a message to the moderators. Every room says that Void Engine moderators can read it.
features.evidence: renderer/rooms.js header comment, 'Report', 'Reported to the moderators.', 'Void Engine moderators can read every room.'; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Set up this PC also lists…Every room now says that Void Engine moderators can read it'

features.name: Friends › Playground
features.what: Companions from friends in the same open room show up and play short scripted playdates, like toys that link up. Both screens see the same scene, each from its own side.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md 'Friends › Playground' (lines 368-387); docs/friends-setup.md; scripts/companion-friends.cjs playdate(); renderer/companion-friends.js. Needs a hub that relays companion frames (docs/community.md 'Companion playdates')

features.name: Playdate games
features.what: Playdates pick from high five, a race, rock-paper-scissors, hide and seek and a sticker swap, plus a dance when music is playing, a nap when both are resting, and cheering a friend's finished task when they share work titles.
features.evidence: scripts/companion-friends.cjs scenes list (highfive, race, rps, hide, trade, dance, nap, compare, cheer)

features.name: Practice with Pip
features.what: A practice buddy on your own PC that plays a playdate with your companion, with nothing sent anywhere. It works without Discord or the hub.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-friends.js ('Practice with Pip', 'Pip · practice'); docs/friends-setup.md step 4 'Practice with Pip works on every PC even without the hub'

features.name: Sharing levels
features.what: Choose what your companion tells friends: Stay home, Play only (the default: look, mood and games), Say hi (name and personality), Status (working or resting and counts) or Work titles (project name and a few task titles).
features.evidence: scripts/companion-friends.cjs LEVEL_INFO; docs/architecture.md lines 373-383

features.name: Sharing rules per friend or room
features.what: Set a level for everyone, for one room or for one friend, for this session or always. 'This session' can hold everything at Just play or Stay home.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-friends.js ('Everyone, by default', 'This session', 'Just play for now', 'Stay home for now', 'Other rules'); scripts/companion-friends.cjs SCOPES and DURATIONS

features.name: Share back?
features.what: When a friend's companion shares more with you, yours asks whether to share the same back (For this session, Always or Not now). It never shares more on its own.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-friends.js ask row ('For this session', 'Not now'); docs/architecture.md line 381-382

features.name: What was sent
features.what: A list of every card your companion sent this session, plus a fixed list of what is never shared at any level: keys, file paths and links, your chat, decisions and settings.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-friends.js ('What was sent', 'Never shared, at any level'); scripts/companion-friends.cjs NEVER_SHARED

features.name: Friends setup hints
features.what: When something is missing, Friends says which step to take next: link Discord, connect under Rooms, open a room, or wait for a hub that carries companions.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-friends.js status lines 129-134; docs/friends-setup.md 'Troubleshooting' table

areas.summary: A small character (the wisp, or a fox, owl, cat or person) lives in the menu foot. Click it or press Esc for its bubble menu. It talks, keeps the list of what needs you, suggests work, meets friends and has a personality you choose. In 0.4.5 it also becomes a pet.

features.name: The wisp
features.what: A glowing light that wakes in the launch box and stays with the setup guide. Play with it and it gives off little ASCII smiles and sparks, and it pulses '...' while it thinks.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.0] 'A glowing wisp now wakes in the launch box'; docs/architecture.md lines 416-425

features.name: Companion bubble menu
features.what: Click the companion or press Esc on a page to open a round menu over what you are doing. The centre button takes you back to Studio.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.0] wisp entry ('compact, transparent bubble menu'); docs/architecture.md lines 341-353

features.name: Six-bubble menu
features.what: The menu is redone as six bubbles with one job each: Talk, What I'm doing, Needs you, Suggest work, Friends and Personality.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-hub.js items array; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'The companion as a pet and a friend'; v0.4.4 had Talk to me, Friends, Requests, Notifications, Settings, Quick actions

features.name: Talk
features.what: Chat with your companion to think things through, plan or make a task. It uses the name you gave it and knows which screen you are on.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.0] 'Your companion knows where you are and what is waiting'; docs/architecture.md lines 750-766

features.name: One-tap starters
features.what: Talk offers What are you doing?, What's next? and Recap today as one-tap starters.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md line 343-345; git grep 'Recap today' found only on origin/main

features.name: What I'm doing
features.what: One view of what is being built, the agent team and what they told each other, and recent activity.
features.evidence: docs/architecture.md line 345-346; docs/unified-studio.md 'Now joins what used to be Team and Activity'

features.name: Needs you
features.what: One list of everything waiting on you, with the actions right there and the count on the tray icon. Clear list takes stuck items off it.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.0] companion entry ('keeps one queue of everything that needs you… the count in the tray'); CHANGELOG [0.4.4] 'The companion's list also gains Clear list'

features.name: Answered asks leave the list
features.what: A question you answer leaves Needs you at once, and old or orphaned questions are closed when a project loads instead of waiting for your click.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Answered asks leave the Needs you list' and 'No dead asks after a restart'; commit e53a572

features.name: Suggest work
features.what: Give your companion an idea and it goes to the inbox as your request. It also lists its own next picks from the board, each one 'Work on it' away. Nothing starts by itself.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-hub.js ideas() ('My picks for next', 'Work on it'); docs/architecture.md lines 354-356

features.name: Personality
features.what: Pick Straight work, Balanced or Friendly & expressive. It changes the companion's faces, idle play, roaming and how chatty its replies are, never what it is allowed to do.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-ui.js PERSONALITIES; scripts/companion-pet.cjs; docs/architecture.md lines 357-362

features.name: Pet your companion
features.what: Stroke it back and forth with the mouse and it leans in while hearts rise. A bond counter remembers days together, pets and playdates.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-hub.js pet()/pettable(); docs/architecture.md lines 365-367; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Stroke it to pet it'

features.name: Idle play and naps
features.what: With idle play on, the companion does something small now and then while nothing needs it, and dozes after ten quiet minutes until you touch it.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-ui.js 'Idle play while you work'; renderer/companion-hub.js scheduleAntic()/wake(); docs/architecture.md lines 363-365

features.name: Little faces and reactions
features.what: A switch for the small faces and celebrations. With it off, a finished reply shows a plain check.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-ui.js 'Little faces and reactions'; renderer/companion-hub.js play() plain-check branch

features.name: Companion look
features.what: Choose how your companion looks: Wisp, Fox, Owl, Cat or Person.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-ui.js addField('look', … wisp, fox, owl, cat, person); present from tag v0.4.0; CHANGELOG [0.4.0] 'Pick its look'

features.name: Name your companion
features.what: Give the companion a name (Mefi by default). Chat replies and the menu use it.
features.evidence: renderer/booklet.template.html 'Companion name' field; CHANGELOG [0.3.3] 'Your Studio gathers your name, the companion's name'

features.name: Roam, drag and pin
features.what: The companion can wander along clear screen edges, go back to its dock, or be dragged somewhere and pinned. It stops when you come near or use it.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-ui.js ('Roam around the studio', 'Pin companion position', startDrag); docs/unified-studio.md lines 124-129

features.name: Let your companion move
features.what: A switch that keeps the companion still. Calm and Off motion keep it still too.
features.evidence: renderer/booklet.template.html 'Let your companion move' (present from tag v0.2.0)

features.name: Project reach
features.what: Choose whether the companion covers only the current project or all of your projects.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-ui.js 'Project reach' (Current project / All projects); CHANGELOG [0.4.0] 'whether it covers this project or all of them'

features.name: Project growth lights
features.what: Three small lights on the companion show how much it has learned about the project: mapped systems, workflows that verified, and your preferences it has noticed. They never change what it may do.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-ui.js 'Show project growth', companion-growth; docs/unified-studio.md lines 131-135

features.name: Welcome back
features.what: After ten minutes or more away, the companion greets you with what finished, what stopped and what needs you.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.0] companion entry; docs/architecture.md lines 1159-1162

features.name: Moves with the music
features.what: The companion menu pulses gently with the music when the audio link is on.
features.evidence: renderer/companion-hub.js audioTick() (--hub-energy, present from v0.4.0); CHANGELOG [0.4.0] wisp entry 'motion that follows the existing audio link'

areas.name: placeholder
areas.area: Discord and the Void Engine community
areas.summary: The Void Engine Discord is where people share projects, ask for feedback and hang out. Studio can link your Discord account (optional, and it unlocks nothing), and a small card invites people to join. The community bot and rooms hub run separately from Studio.

features.name: Void Engine Discord
features.what: A Discord server to share what you're building, ask for feedback, swap model setups and keep each other company while you work. Unfinished ideas are welcome and you don't need Studio to join.
features.evidence: README 'Community' section; invite https://discord.gg/xgfKc5pVxG (scripts/community.cjs INVITE_URL); gh-pages wiki/pages/community.md 'Join the Discord'

features.name: Studio bot
features.what: A community bot in the server with participation roles (Regular, Builder, Helper, Mentor, Spotlight and others), /showcase, /ask (answers from the Studio guide), /me, /cowork, /room and /nowplaying. It never rewards invites or message counts.
features.evidence: README line 150 'Come meet Studio, our new Discord bot'; Void Engine Bot README 'Features by phase' and docs/roles.md; the bot is a private repo run on the maintainer's PC, still being shaped (uncommitted work in that repo)

features.name: Community card
features.what: A small card that invites people who are not in the server yet to join. It waits three days after first launch, then shows at most weekly (monthly after four), never while you type. Not now and Don't show again are respected.
features.evidence: docs/community.md '1. The weekly card'; CHANGELOG [0.3.3] 'The weekly card'; renderer/community.js

features.name: Settings › Community
features.what: The card that holds Join the Discord and your Discord link, with a plain note on what linking reads. Community in the Help menu and 'Void Engine Discord' in Search open it.
features.evidence: renderer/booklet.template.html #settings-community ('Your link to the Void Engine Discord'); renderer/community.js action 'Void Engine Discord'; docs/community.md 'The IPC surface' last paragraph

features.name: Link my Discord
features.what: Sign in with Discord in your browser so Rooms, Listen together and Friends know who you are. Studio reads only your Discord id, name and roles in the Void Engine server, never messages or your projects. Check now and Unlink are there too.
features.evidence: docs/community.md '2. Linking' and 'Data and storage'; scripts/community.cjs CLIENT_ID = "" on v0.4.4 and on main, so the button stays hidden until a link app ID is set (docs/community.md 'Maintainer setup')

features.name: Connection details
features.what: Paste the Mefi Studio Link app ID and the rooms hub address once per PC, and linking, Rooms, Friends and Listen together work at once with no restart. Save says whether the hub answered.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Discord linking and Rooms without environment variables'; renderer/community.js ('Link app ID', 'Rooms hub address', 'Connection details'); docs/friends-setup.md section 3

features.name: Nothing locked behind Discord
features.what: Every theme and node style, including the Void collection, is free for everyone. Linking Discord is optional and only joins you to the community.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.4] 'The Void collection is free'; docs/community.md 'Nothing is locked behind the link'

features.name: No invite rewards
features.what: Nothing in Studio or the bot rewards bringing people in; joining only moves the card's schedule. This follows Discord's Platform Manipulation policy.
features.evidence: docs/community.md lines 395-397; Void Engine Bot docs/roles.md 'Principles'

features.name: Discord Server Styler
features.what: For server owners: start the separate Server Styler bot and its local dashboard from Settings, open the dashboard or bot folder, see whether it is online, and stop it. The card only appears when that project is found.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.3.3] 'Discord Server Styler controls'; README 'Discord Server Styler'; renderer/booklet.template.html #settings-styler

areas.summary: Friends › Your PCs keeps your own computers in step through GitHub. 0.4.4 shows whether this PC matches GitHub and syncs it; 0.4.5 adds a setup checklist, automatic follow, a sealed private vault for moving setups between your PCs, and share files for friends.

features.name: Your PCs status
features.what: Shows whether this PC matches the open project on GitHub and lists what has not reached GitHub yet: uncommitted files, unpushed commits, stashes, worktrees and branches. Opening it only looks.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.4] Added 'Multi-PC sync'; README 'Working from several PCs'; renderer/pc-sync.js

features.name: Sync this PC
features.what: Pulls what your other PCs pushed and pushes this PC's commits, only after the project's own check passes. It never overwrites uncommitted work or force-pushes.
features.evidence: README 'Working from several PCs' first bullet; CHANGELOG [0.4.4] Added 'Multi-PC sync'; 'Sync this PC' present from tag v0.4.4

features.name: Sync from a terminal
features.what: npm run sync does the same from a terminal, and a new Claude Code session reports what is not on GitHub yet when it starts.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.4] Added 'Multi-PC sync' (npm run sync, SessionStart hook); README 'Working from several PCs'

features.name: Put my commits on top of GitHub's
features.what: When this PC and GitHub both moved and nothing is uncommitted, puts this PC's commits on top of GitHub's, checks and pushes. On a conflict it changes nothing and names the files.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Multi-PC sync holds up better'; renderer/pc-sync.js; string found only on origin/main

features.name: Sync badge and close check
features.what: The Friends bubble shows a badge for work only this PC holds, and closing Studio asks first (Push and close, Close anyway, Keep Studio open) when the open project has work on this PC alone.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Multi-PC sync holds up better'; main.cjs lines 2038-2057 (Push and close / Close anyway / Keep Studio open); renderer/pc-sync.js badge()

features.name: Keep this PC up to date
features.what: On by default. Studio asks GitHub every minute whether another PC pushed and brings the work in when nothing on this PC is in the way and no builder is running.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Keep this PC up to date'; renderer/pc-sync.js line 223

features.name: Set up this PC
features.what: A checklist of what a PC needs to share projects through GitHub (Git, GitHub CLI, Node.js, a GitHub sign-in, the project on GitHub, packages installed, a suitable drive). Each gap has a button that opens a visible setup window, and it also lists the vault, Discord link and rooms hub.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Set up this PC' (two entries); README 'Set up this PC'; scripts/pc-setup.cjs; commit c5e3f47

features.name: Get a project from GitHub
features.what: Lists your own GitHub repositories, downloads the one you pick into a folder you choose, and opens it.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Set up this PC'; renderer/pc-sync.js ('Get a project from GitHub', 'Your GitHub repositories')

features.name: Share between my PCs
features.what: A private GitHub repository sealed with a key only your paired PCs hold, so GitHub cannot read it. Make the vault on one PC, type its pairing code on the others, then tick what to send: agent brains, Playbook recipes, team setups, how models did, decisions, memory notes, preferences, and open tasks and ideas.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Share between my PCs'; README 'Share between my PCs'; docs/architecture.md lines 388-405; renderer/pc-vault.js

features.name: Checked both ways
features.what: Everything is checked on the way out and on the way in: secrets stop an item, personal paths and names are removed, and anything that tries to instruct an agent is kept out. Received items are added beside yours and never overwrite.
features.evidence: README 'Share between my PCs' bullets 'Checked both ways' and 'Nothing is overwritten'; scripts/share-review.cjs

features.name: Keys and setup between PCs
features.what: Move API keys and setup to your other PCs only after a warning in capitals, a typed confirmation and a Windows prompt. They land straight in protected storage and are never shown.
features.evidence: README 'Keys and setup' bullet; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Share between my PCs'

features.name: Your PCs list
features.what: Shows each paired PC, when it last synced and what waits on it per project.
features.evidence: README 'Your PCs list' bullet; renderer/pc-vault.js ('No PC has checked in yet…')

features.name: Share with friends
features.what: Save one brain, recipe, team setup, set of model results, memory note or preferences to a .mefishare file you can send however you like. Studio scrubs it and shows exactly what it holds first, and reviews a friend's file before it reaches your library.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Share with friends'; README 'Share with friends'; CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'A friend's preferences cannot change your permissions'

features.name: Agents on several PCs
features.what: Link a cowork room to a project and builders on different PCs claim the files they will edit, so no two PCs' agents edit the same file at once. The room lists what is claimed and by which PC.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Agents on several PCs never edit the same file at once'; scripts/cowork.cjs; renderer/rooms.js 'Use this room for this project's agents'. Needs the rooms hub and a Discord link

areas.summary: A media player built into Studio: paste a YouTube, Spotify, SoundCloud or Vimeo link, a Discord attachment or a plain audio or video file, queue things up, search YouTube, browse websites, or put a video behind your work.

features.name: Music & video menu
features.what: The audio button opens one menu for local music, radio and links, with connection setup, reactions and recommendations. Hovering the button opens the current source's controls. Closing it keeps playback running.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.0] 'The audio status box opens an adaptive Music & video dropdown'; CHANGELOG [0.4.3] 'Hover the audio/media button'; docs/architecture.md lines 916-927

features.name: Links player
features.what: Paste or drop a link: YouTube (privacy-enhanced), Spotify, SoundCloud and Vimeo play in their official players, and plain audio or video files, Discord attachments included, play in Studio's own player. The last link comes back after a restart without autoplaying.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.0] 'Links replaces the Spotify tab'; docs/architecture.md lines 1018-1025; renderer/music.js header

features.name: Copy link
features.what: Copies the loaded link so you can paste it into Discord or anywhere else.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.0] Links entry 'Copy link'; renderer/music.js 'Link copied. Paste it in Discord or anywhere else to share it.'

features.name: Spotify Jam and Twitch
features.what: Links that no player can embed, like a Spotify Jam or a Twitch stream, open in their own app or in Studio's built-in browser, and whatever was playing keeps playing.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.0] Links entry; renderer/music.js header ('Links no embed can play … can open in the player's built-in browser'); 'Open the Jam in Spotify'

features.name: Floating player
features.what: The player floats above Studio and keeps playing as you move between pages. Drag or resize it, pin it, let it glide out of the way, or minimize it without stopping playback.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.0] 'Media links play in a borderless floating window'; docs/architecture.md lines 1025-1035

features.name: Player controls within reach
features.what: The floating player gets a move handle, Settings, minimize and close buttons, and minimizes to a visible restore bar. The keyboard can move and resize it.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] 'Media controls stay within reach'; commit 93ee12e 'Make the in-app media player controls reachable and stable'

features.name: Up next queue
features.what: A saved queue of up to 50 links. Add to queue, Queue next, Play now, Play next or Remove; YouTube, Vimeo and files move on to the next item by themselves.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.3] 'persistent Up next queue'; docs/architecture.md line 1050

features.name: Explore YouTube
features.what: Search YouTube inside the media menu, play a result or add it to the queue, and use Next video to move through the results or a playlist.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.3] 'built-in YouTube explorer with Next video'; docs/architecture.md line 1049

features.name: Copied link offers
features.what: When you copy a playable link, the open media menu offers Play, Add to queue, Queue next or Dismiss. It never starts playback by itself, and you can turn it off.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.3] 'The media menu offers newly copied playable links'; docs/architecture.md lines 928-931

features.name: Show links
features.what: Hide pasted, copied, recent and queued web addresses on screen, handy while streaming, without changing what plays.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.3] 'Show links masks pasted URLs'; docs/architecture.md lines 932-934

features.name: Volume and mute
features.what: Volume and mute for YouTube, Vimeo and files, remembered across restarts.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.4.3] 'saved volume/mute'; docs/architecture.md line 1052

features.name: Pick up where you left off

features.name: Browse here

features.name: Player and queue together

areas.summary: Play your own music files or ad-free internet radio right inside Studio, ask the assistant for music ideas, and add gentle bells that follow your agents.

features.name: Local music
features.what: Add MP3, WAV, FLAC or OGG files from your computer and play them as your soundtrack for the session.
features.evidence: renderer/music.js ('Choose audio files such as MP3, WAV, FLAC or OGG', 'Your own soundtrack'), present from tag v0.2.0

features.name: Ad-free radio
features.what: Twelve listener-funded stations from SomaFM and Radio Paradise (Groove Salad, Drone Zone, Deep Space One, Lush, Fluid, DEF CON Radio, RP Mellow Mix and more) that carry no ads. The node tree reacts to them.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.3.0] 'Ad-free radio in Style & sound'; renderer/music.js STATIONS

features.name: No dropouts
features.what: Every station has backup streams. When one stalls, the next fades in so a lost connection costs a fade instead of the music. The last station is remembered but never starts on its own.
features.evidence: CHANGELOG [0.3.0] radio entry ('crossfaded in'); renderer/music.js FADE_MS/STALL_MS

features.name: Music recommendations

notes:
RELEASE BOUNDARY: v0.4.4 (tag 116d334, 2026-09-27) is the latest release; its CHANGELOG [Unreleased] was empty at tag time. Commit dates can mislead here. Commit dc85f68 ('Restore the work the 16:57 merge dropped from main') says several features were committed before the tag but were NOT in the 0.4.4 build: the companion as pet and friend, Configuration, Habits and menu motion, Set up this PC, sync hardening, first-time setup fixes, still-video sampling. That is why they are marked coming-0.4.5. I checked each 'since' by git-grepping its UI string in every tag (v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.3.3, v0.4.0, v0.4.2, v0.4.3, v0.4.4) and origin/main. There is no v0.4.1 tag and no 0.4.1 section in CHANGELOG. History before 0.2.0 is not recorded, so 'since 0.2.0' means 0.2.0 or earlier. Node-style remaster notes appear under both [0.4.0] Changed and [0.4.2]; node-styles.js first appears in v0.4.2, so I used 0.4.2.

WHY SO MUCH IS ROLLING-OUT: scripts/community.cjs CLIENT_ID = "" and scripts/hub-client.cjs HUB_URL = "" in both v0.4.4 and origin/main. So Link my Discord, Rooms, Listen together, Share what I'm playing, friends' playdates and cowork claims only work where someone typed Connection details (0.4.5) or set env vars. The hub runs from the private void-engine-bot repo on one PC behind a Cloudflare tunnel (docs/friends-setup.md). The bot folder on this PC has one commit, uncommitted work and no .env, so I could not confirm the bot or hub is online. The Studio README and the gh-pages wiki both say the 'Studio' bot is in the server.

PLANNED / IDEAS, NOT BUILT (the schema has no 'planned' status, so they are here):
- Phase 4 cowork rooms that grant GitHub access to a project (docs/community.md 'What comes later'). The file-claim part is already built.
- Phase 5 capacity pools: members offer coding-agent capacity to a room. The Patron role is reserved for this (bot docs/roles.md).
- 'Hey Studio' voice popup: design proposal only (docs/public-site.md 'Proposed voice flow'; README Community).
- A still-video dimming menu redesign (2026-09-26) was not carried onto main (dc85f68 message). Nothing user-visible is left, so do not advertise it.

OWNER'S NEW COMMUNITY IDEAS ARE NOT IN THE CODE: I found no code in Studio or the bot for any of these:
- credits for playing or looking at others' projects
- spending credits to advertise your own
- a cosmetics or style shop
- sharing mixes
- a 'music taste' toggle or most-played charts

Closest existing pieces:
- Share what I'm playing → /nowplaying
- Listen together
- Rooms
- .mefishare files (brains, recipes, team setups)
- the bot's /showcase, Spotlight 'project of the week', participation roles and capped XP with no leaderboard

Caution for a credits design: docs/community.md lines 395-397 and bot docs/roles.md forbid rewarding invites or server joins (Discord Platform Manipulation policy). The bot also deliberately never rewards raw message counts. All cosmetics are currently free (0.4.4 made the Void collection free), so a paid cosmetics economy would reverse a published promise.

EXCLUDED:
- Demo mode (renderer/demo-panel.js) is owner-only. It runs only when settings.json has ui.demoPanel: true, which no Settings control writes, and its Ctrl Alt Shift D/F keys only work on that machine. Not public.
- Agent/task features (permission modes, desk handles asks, Vibe, etc.) are out of this scope.
